key_idea: Take logs: log price(A,x) = P_A + (x-1)*M_A + I_x is linear in the unknowns, so a query is determined iff its coefficient vector lies in the row space of the known equations.
sketch: Unknowns are P_A, M_A per commodity and prefix log-inflations I_2..I_y (at most 209). Each known price gives one equation and each known inflation gives I_{x+1}-I_x = log r. Gauss-Jordan to reduced row echelon form with long doubles and partial pivoting (coefficients are small integers, eps 1e-9), then reduce each query vector by the pivot rows: if a non-pivot coordinate remains it is undetermined (-1.0), else print exp of the combined right-hand side. About 1000 x 209 x 209 operations. Pitfall: a query can be determined even when neither modifier nor inflation is individually known. Verified against exact rational rank computations.
